name: National mysticism
summary: National mysticism raises the nation to a sacred status, treating it as a divine or spiritual reality with its own eternal destiny rather than a mere political arrangement. Its adherents prize the nation's antiquity, language, soil and people, put duty and sacrifice above individual interest, and distrust rationalism, liberal democracy and universalism. Where it took organised form, as in the Volkisch movement and the Romanian Legion, it joined this to charismatic leadership, a cult of martyrs, spiritual rebirth and antisemitism.
scope: The family of nationalisms that sanctify the nation, represented by Fichte's Addresses to the German Nation (1808) as the philosophical root, the Germanic Volkisch movement and its Ariosophic offshoots, and Codreanu's Romanian Legionary movement as organised exemplars. Italian Fascist mysticism, Nazi state occultism and unrelated religious nationalisms are excluded. Because the movements wrote little on economics or policy detail, many answers on economics and modern issues are low-confidence inferences from their principles.

keyFigures.name: Johann Gottlieb Fichte
keyFigures.role: Philosopher named by the Wikipedia article as the thinker who presented the nation as a divine entity

keyFigures.name: Corneliu Zelea Codreanu
keyFigures.role: Founder and Captain of the Romanian Legionary movement, which called itself a spiritual school for national rebirth

sources.title: Addresses to the German Nation
sources.author: Johann Gottlieb Fichte, 1808 (Jones and Turnbull translation)
sources.usedFor: The nation as arising out of the divine, immortality through the people, national education, the living language, state as a means, readiness to die for the nation, self-reliance.

sources.title: National mysticism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Definition: the nation raised to numen; Fichte, Germanic mysticism and pseudohistorical claims of antiquity.

sources.title: Volkisch movement
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: The mystical Volk, racial hierarchy, occultism, anti-rationalism, rural idealism, antisemitism and the call for a Volkisch dictatorship.

sources.title: Iron Guard
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Legionary mystical nationalism: Orthodox elements, spiritual rebirth, New Man, martyrdom, leader cult, anti-democracy, antisemitism, peasant ideal and absence of economic program.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Mystical nationalists wrote little on health policy; a duty to the national body could favour state care, but the Legion stressed spiritual over material programs.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Iron Guard had no consistent economic program, so no position on wage floors can be documented.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Legion rejected capitalism as overly materialistic and favoured a communal or national economy, so it would not credit free markets with the best allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: With no worked-out economic program, adherents split between national-economy collectivism and peasant smallholding; nothing in the sources settles ownership of utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The sources record no tax doctrine; the Legion's hostility to capitalists is largely tied to blaming Jews for economic ills, not to progressive taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Völkisch thought wanted organic national solidarity over class interests, but separate unions were not a theme; inferred only.

property-fundamental.rationale: Mystical nationalism subordinates property to the nation's destiny but also idealises the peasant landholder; sources do not settle how firm property rights should be.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Hostility to capitalist materialism suggests support for national control of big business, though this is inferred, not a stated program.

cut-welfare.rationale: Obligation to the national community suggests care for the people, but welfare policy is not discussed; inferred from the organic view of the nation.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Legion's communal economy is vague and never specified worker ownership; no documented position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Authoritarian nationalists accepted extensive policing against perceived internal enemies, but terrorism-specific surveillance is an inference.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Völkisch and Legionary ideals of purity, discipline and spiritual renewal sit badly with drug legalisation; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Open antisemitism was central to the Iron Guard and Völkisch movement, so adherents would resist laws restricting speech against alien groups.

strong-leader.rationale: The Legion rested on Codreanu's charismatic leadership, and Völkisch writers wanted heroes rather than calculating politicians to lead.

state-harmful.rationale: For Fichte the state is a necessary framework for the nation's eternal development, so calling it harmful is foreign to the tradition.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun policy is not addressed; militant movements prized martial virtue but also state order.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Legion's cult of martial sacrifice and the nationalist demand for national strength imply support for strong armed forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Spiritual purification of the nation and the Legion's moral rhetoric imply opposition; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Fichte's nation is a single organic whole realised through the state, favouring national unity over localism, though Völkisch ruralists prized homeland.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is not documented; the New Man ideal of spiritual self-purification pulls one way, retribution against enemies the other.

traditional-family.rationale: Völkisch movements treated the Volk as an organic community rooted in ancestry and rural life, and the family as its cell.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Völkisch and Orthodox Legionary traditionalism are hostile to departures from inherited moral order; inferred but strongly implied.

abortion-legal.rationale: Concern for the nation's continuance across generations, as in Fichte, and Orthodox Legionary religiosity imply opposition.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Legion fused Orthodox Christianity with nationalism, and national mysticism treats the nation as sacred; Völkisch pagan strands would want a different religion, hence not strongest.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Völkisch thought ranked peoples hierarchically and prized the Volk's essence, so programs correcting historical injustice to other groups would be rejected.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Volk is seen as an intuitive, spiritual essence rooted in nature, and the movement was anti-rationalist and anti-modern, so constructivism would be rejected.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Fichte's Addresses make the nation's distinct character and language the object to be preserved against fusion with foreign peoples.

gradual-change.rationale: The Legion sought spiritual rebirth and a revolutionary New Man, not gradual institutional reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Fichte feared the nation's fusion with foreign peoples and the Völkisch movement treated outsiders as corrupting; immigration as such was not their main subject.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: A nation held to be a divine, self-contained order has no reason to cede authority to international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-capitalist materialism and a national economy suggest scepticism, though trade is not discussed.

nation-first.rationale: Fichte's Addresses treat the nation's survival and its own development as the highest purpose, above other ends.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: A national mystic prizes the nation's own mission and sacrifice; universal human-rights interventions are not a theme.

open-borders.rationale: Fichte warned against the nation's fusion with foreign peoples, and Völkisch thinkers saw outsiders as threats to the Volk's purity.

limit-growth.rationale: Völkisch nature romanticism opposed industrial evils, but also wanted a numerous, strong Volk; the sources do not settle growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate change was not an issue for these movements; reverence for land and nature gives some pull, indifference to technocratic programs the other.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Völkisch thought rejected scientistic and rationalistic modernity in favour of spiritual renewal.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Legion sought national spiritual rebirth by revolutionary means including violence and assassination, though it did not frame this as revolution in the left's sense.

experts-over-public.rationale: Mysticism puts intuition, faith and the Volk's instinct above rational expertise; leadership by heroes, not technocrats.

central-planning.rationale: The Legion's communal economy is unspecified and no planning doctrine is documented.

socialized-markets.rationale: No documented position; the Legion rejected capitalism but also communism.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; Völkisch back-to-the-land populism touched land reform but not this tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents give no consistent view.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional payments clash with the ethic of service and sacrifice, but the question is anachronistic; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: A national economy rejecting international capitalism suggests protectionism; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No documented economic doctrine; Fichte's state is a means to national development, which leaves room but no explicit demand.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Glorification of peasant landholding and rural life suggests a smallholder ideal; the sources do not state it as program.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The Legion rejected communism and its ideal of a classless stateless economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Völkisch antisemitism targeted finance, but banking structure is not discussed; no clear stance.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Interwar corporatism appealed to many nationalist movements, but the Iron Guard had no consistent economic program.

one-party-rule.rationale: The DVFP called for a völkisch dictatorship and the Legion rejected democratic pluralism; the Legion later ruled in a coalition, so only moderate support.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Völkisch writers idealised the Holy Roman Empire's hierarchy, but the Legion was hostile to the Romanian royal court in practice; adherents split.

democracy-best.rationale: Codreanu dismissed universal democratic values as Jewish inventions.

direct-votes.rationale: Rule by heroes and natural elites is preferred to any popular decision-making, though Völkisch thinkers spoke of a primitive democracy.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power belongs to the communist tradition the Legion opposed.

right-to-secede.rationale: The nation is held to be an indivisible eternal whole; splitting it would be an offence against it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Völkisch thinkers wanted natural elites and heroic leaders, and the Legion put a charismatic Captain at the top.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Legion practised assassination and cultivated martyrdom through its Death Squad, and treated sacrificial struggle as spiritual duty.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Iron Guard's ultra-nationalism was steeped in First World War experience and a cult of sacrifice; Fichte also valued readiness to die for the nation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Legionary ideology inserted Orthodox elements into politics; Völkisch strands wanted a Germanised church or a pagan one tied to the Volk.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Legion was spiritual rather than legalist, and Völkisch pagans had no scripture to follow; nation-based law is more likely.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Fichte treats the state as essential vehicle of the nation; privatising defence conflicts with sacred national unity.

military-superiority.rationale: Ultra-nationalism of the Legion and national self-assertion imply strength vis-a-vis rivals; not an explicit program.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Volk is an ancestral essence, and Völkisch racism treated Jews as an alien people.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Legion opposed Marxism and saw history as the nation's spiritual struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Völkisch hierarchism and natural elites contradict equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents prize their own people's homeland, which pulls toward land-rootedness for all peoples but is not stated.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Völkisch and national-superiority ideas weigh against admitting such obligations; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Mystical nationalism centres on the single nation as a sacred whole, though pan-Germanic strands wanted union of kin peoples.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Fichte held that self-seeking had destroyed itself and wanted love and service of the nation to drive the will.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Fichte demanded sacrifice for the nation, even readiness to die, and the Legion's ideal man seeks nothing for himself.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Völkisch thinkers idealised a primordial cosmic order and saw the Volk as an expression of a landscape's soul.

limit-population.rationale: Fichte's hope rests on the eternal continuance of the people, so a numerous, growing nation is wanted.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Völkisch movement opposed the evils of industrialisation and atomised modern life.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Anti-modern and anti-rationalist Völkisch outlook rejects disruption for its own sake.

human-enhancement.rationale: Spiritual purification and organic nature romanticism disfavour technological body modification; anachronistic.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by intuition, heroes and faith is the opposite of rule by calculation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A question from the digital age that national mystics never faced; their authoritarian instincts and their stress on national security tilt one way and a distrust of the state's rivals the other, so nothing settles it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Völkisch thinkers romanticised the Holy Roman Empire and ancient Germanic tradition, yet the Legion also looked to a revolutionary new man, hence not stronger.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement rejects rationalism and holds faith in the sacred nation above calculation.

direct-action.rationale: The Legion used assassinations and street violence alongside elections, so adherents favoured direct, sacrificial action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Legionary stress on self-purification and spiritual school suggests methods should embody the aim; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Back-to-the-land ruralism is agrarian, not a call to abandon agriculture.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: This is a communist aim of dissolving class-bound occupations; the Legion fought communism and its peasant-and-nation ideal presumes distinct callings within an organic whole.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is a communist principle; the Legion rejected communism.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-capitalist rhetoric of the Legion but no developed economic doctrine.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist theory was rejected, but the Legion blamed Jews for economic exploitation of Romanians; mixed.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship is Marxist and the Legion was anti-communist.

collective-farming.rationale: Collective farming conflicts with the glorified peasant smallholder and with the Legion's anti-communism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist theory rejected; the Legion's critique of capitalism was moral and tied to Jews, not to imperialist-war theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: The nation and its state are sacred and demand sacrifice, so taxation as theft is alien.

harm-principle.rationale: Fichte's education aimed to shape the will, not leave individuals to their own choices; the community may regulate far more than harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Fichte denied that individual injury is healed by the nation's glory, but still placed the whole above the individual; group and nation have standing.

conscription.rationale: Fichte held a man must be ready to die that the nation may live, which carries naturally to compulsory service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Fichte and the Legion bind the individual to the nation as to a sacred whole, so treating the freedom to leave as the main check on rulers contradicts the bond they hold sacred.

state-as-business.rationale: Fichte's state serves the eternal development of the nation, not commercial service to customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Fichte's education towards a good will resembles positive freedom, but material means are not discussed.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anti-rationalist and anti-intellectual strands might suspect them, but the sources record no such claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racism was central to the Völkisch movement, with Aryan or German racial hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Völkisch thinkers imagined an organic, hierarchical order rather than party democracy; corporatist specifics are not documented.

total-state.rationale: Fichte wanted a total transformation of education to make the nation, but the state is a means; the Legion stressed spirit more than state.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Legion described itself as a spiritual school aiming at the spiritual rebirth of the nation, and Fichte likewise called for a new world and new self.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ultra-nationalism and Völkisch pan-Germanism imply expansion, but it is not stated as core.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Legionary loyalty to the Captain was personal, but feudal vassalage is not the model.

bound-labor.rationale: Peasant idealisation does not extend to serfdom; the Volk's free rooted farmers are the ideal.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: National mystics distrust rationalist claims to neutrality in favour of intuition and the Volk's spirit, but they do not argue the left-style thesis that truth merely reflects power, so the sources give no clear stance.

universal-morality.rationale: The Volk's essence and spiritual intuition, not universal reason, grounds values; yet Orthodox Christians held universal truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Fichte's nation is a single whole under one divine law of development, with no room for balancing rival interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The Iron Guard and Völkisch antisemites saw Jews as alien; the views on a Jewish state are not documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources on national mysticism say nothing about diaspora return; a blood-and-soil Volk might welcome kin, but ancestry-based exclusion could equally limit it, so this is left open.

revive-national-language.rationale: Fichte treated the living national language as the root of the people's creativity, so language is vital to the nation.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Volkisch and Legionary ideal is a hierarchical organic order led by heroes, so democratic votes over firm management would not be favoured, though economic organisation is not detailed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Fichte wanted a single national education, not market choice among schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Iron Guard had no consistent economic program and the sources record no fiscal doctrine, so the question is left neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: The Legion rejected capitalism and put the nation above individual economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: The Legion's New Man and Codreanu's example as Captain aimed at moral leadership; Völkisch writers asked for heroes as leaders.

national-self-determination.rationale: Fichte's Addresses grounded the nation's right to exist and develop by its own law.

force-without-un.rationale: The United Nations is anachronistic; nationalists accept national force when required.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Völkisch movement explicitly rejected scientistic and rationalistic thinking in favour of intuitive, spiritual renewal.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Concern for the Volk and its exclusion of aliens implies benefits for members only.

work-for-welfare.rationale: An ethic of service, discipline and labour for the national community suggests conditioning support on work, but this is inferred rather than stated in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Organic Volk community over class conflict; Legion opposed Marxism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: National mystics revere ancestral antiquity and the nation's inherited monuments, as in Volkisch romanticising of ancient Germanic tradition, so they would not sacrifice them to novelty.

dominated-front.rationale: Common fronts of states dominated by the West are a theme of other traditions; the sources on national mysticism concentrate on a single sacred nation and do not discuss it.

workers-nation.rationale: The Legion opposed internationalist communism and tied workers to the nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Legion rhetoric stressed masculine virility and women were a small share of members.

ban-interest.rationale: Antisemitic image of finance but no documented ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Völkisch racism prized purity; legal segregation is not specifically documented.

state-class-instrument.rationale: This is the Marxist view of the state, which the Legion opposed; for Fichte the state is a framework for the nation's eternal development, not an instrument of one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy was outside the horizon of these movements, and their agrarian nature reverence and national self-reliance point in opposite directions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: A racial Volk cannot be joined by assimilation in Völkisch thought, but Fichte spoke of cultural absorption; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: Anachronistic, though antisemitic conspiracy views are close.

proportional-representation.rationale: Both the Legion and the Volkisch right rejected party-based parliamentary politics, so a more proportional parliament is not something they seek, though they offer no view on electoral formulas.

national-mission.rationale: Fichte saw Germany's role in the salvation of the world, per his translators; mystical nationalists believe in a national destiny, but mainly cultivation not export of a government form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Volkisch and Legionary writers treated sex roles as natural and the Legion's rhetoric glorified virility, so they would deny that society systematically disadvantages women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The Legion rejected the Francophile elite and parliamentary politicians as corrupt aliens to the nation.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Racial hygiene ideas existed in the Völkisch milieu; not core to mysticism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A movement that glorified martial sacrifice and practised assassination would not accept legal accountability of security forces for past violence; this is inferred as the sources do not discuss it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is not minimal but a framework of national development.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Volkisch offshoots such as the Germanenorden required members to prove they had no non-Aryan blood, showing the movement's concern for racial purity of the Volk.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Volkisch thought ranked Aryans above other peoples and treated Jews as an alien people, so equal standing for all is not held, even though the Orthodox Legion spoke of Christian souls.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question belongs to Marxist debates; national mystics reject international socialism wholesale and the nation as a sacred unit is their frame, so they disagree.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not discuss settler states; a movement centred on a people's rootedness in its soil would be unlikely to call a settled homeland a colonial project.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal civil law for all religions is an issue from other settings; for a national mystic the nation is one community under one law, which leans slightly towards uniformity, but the topic is not documented.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Orthodox Legionaries valued national church membership but conversion law is not documented.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: This is a religious-nationalist cause from the South Asian setting, absent from the Volkisch and Legionary material, so a modest lean against follows from their lack of such taboos.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Legion fused Orthodox Christianity with nationalism and Fichte made national education the nation's lifeline, so religious instruction in state schools would be welcomed.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist thesis about socialist states; the Legion was anti-communist and national mysticism does not use the concept.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy from the nation and its leader, not popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: A strong national economy outside international capitalism suggests mercantilist leanings, but the sources record no trade doctrine, so this is inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The Iron Guard's ideology led to pogroms and antisemitic exclusion; Völkisch alien-people thinking.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Legion cultivated a cult of martyrdom, a Death Squad and assassinations, and Fichte accepted that the nation is worth dying and fighting for, so a ban on initiating force is not part of the creed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Struggle of peoples is natural to racial nationalists; Fichte says new things come from the original nation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Adherents are themselves the likely targets of such bans and regard liberal constitutional orders as alien; this is inferred rather than documented.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Fichte spoke of independence of the nation from foreign rule, but personal republican freedom isn't a theme.

separated-powers.rationale: The Legion and the DVFP rejected liberal parliamentary constitutionalism in favour of leadership by a charismatic head, so checks between rival bodies are not valued.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marxist-Leninist notion; the Legion was a spiritual elite movement but not framed that way.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The sources describe the Legion's economic aims only vaguely and give no priority to the poor as such, but a duty to the whole people is implied.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A housing policy of other political settings that mystical nationalist sources never discuss, so no position can be derived.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: National unity over class conflict is the stance of the Legion and the Volkisch movement, so restrictions on class action are plausible, but labour law itself is not discussed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Fichte's hope for the eternal continuance of the people makes a numerous nation a strength, so blaming population growth for poverty would be rejected.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Volk is treated as a unity of ancestry and spirit, and the movement saw outsiders as corrupting, so diversity is thought to weaken the nation.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Authority should go to heroes and natural elites in Volkisch and Legionary thought, so choosing officials by chance would be rejected.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Legion carried out violence and pogroms against perceived internal enemies, and the DVFP called for a Volkisch dictatorship, so suspending ordinary protections fits.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The sources record no economic program for the Iron Guard, and the topic is outside their documented concerns.

party-controls-media.rationale: Völkisch dictatorship ideas imply control of public communication, but the sources do not describe media policy directly, so this is a low-confidence lean.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Legion fought the army and king at times, yet wanted a nation-wide leader's authority over force; no party-over-state rule is documented.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Because the Volk is defined by ancestry and outsiders are seen as corrosive, adherents would make citizenship hard to obtain, though the exact wait is not documented.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators is not discussed in the sources; the Legion's contempt for corrupt politicians gives some pull toward modest pay but no clear stance.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Legion demanded strict discipline and obedience to the Captain, so members are bound by what the movement decides.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A nation raised to the status of a sacred, divine whole does not share its sovereignty, so supranational union is contrary to its principle.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The leader principle puts command of force in one person, as with Codreanu's Captaincy, but constitutional arrangements are not documented.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Legion drew on Orthodox Christianity, which is governed by bishops, but the question is about church structure, which the sources do not discuss.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Legion borrowed heavily from Orthodoxy but was led by a lay Captain who claimed spiritual rebirth rather than priestly authority, so clergy rule is not its aim.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Fichte demanded readiness to die for the nation and the Legion drew its ultranationalism from the First World War, so working for one's own side's defeat is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: A movement set on spiritual purification of the nation, with moral rhetoric about decadence, would censor art thought to corrupt the people; inferred from its aims.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Leadership by charismatic heroes without fixed terms follows from the leader principle, but the sources do not treat re-election rules.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority comes from the leader and the nation, not from electors' ability to remove officials, so recall mechanisms are not part of the model.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: National mystics stress independence, but the Legion sought alliance with Germany and Italy, so the sources do not give a settled stance.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No housing doctrine appears in the sources; peasant smallholder ideals touch on land, not urban rental.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Legion was a movement of uniformed, devoted volunteers, yet there is no documented demand to replace professional armies with militias.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Völkisch movement promoted back-to-the-land populism idealising rural regions as the home of the original nation, and the Iron Guard glorified peasant culture.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The nation is an eternal whole, and nationalists of the Greater Romania and pan-German strands wanted all members within one state, so reunification fits.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The Legion glorified peasant culture as the embodiment of Romanian genius and rejected the Francophile elite, so degree-holders are seen as detached.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Fichte called Germans the original people with a living language, and Volkisch thought ranked peoples, so equal standing of cultures is rejected.

death-penalty.rationale: The Legion practised killing of enemies and Volkisch ideology prized hardness, so capital punishment for grave crimes would be supported; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Traditionalist, Orthodox and Volkisch views treat sexual morality and sex roles as natural, so school sex and gender-equality teaching would be opposed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Völkisch anti-rationalism and Orthodox religion are compatible with it, but the Volkisch also embraced racial pseudoscience, and the sources never mention it.

restrict-pornography.rationale: A movement committed to purification and spiritual discipline would restrict pornography; the sources imply this without addressing it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Volk is defined by ancestry and Volkisch thought required proof of descent, so citizenship follows blood.

minority-language-support.rationale: Fichte treated the common living language as the basis of the nation, so support for rival languages in state institutions would undermine it.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Minority faiths would be seen as outside the national community, so exemptions would not be granted; inferred from the Legion's Orthodox nationalism.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Fichte and the Legion subordinate individuals to the nation's formation of the will and character, so valuing nonconformity is foreign to them.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The topic is not addressed; Legionary resentment of foreign economic influence gives a faint pull but no documented position.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A postcolonial thesis not found in the sources on national mysticism, whose focus is spiritual rebirth rather than property system reform.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Elected assemblies to rewrite constitutions belong to democratic politics that the Legion and Volkisch right rejected, so they would not favour it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Economic development was not their main aim; restriction of freedoms for national ends is plausible but unspecified.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Their priority is the nation's own survival and development, so duties to the world's poor have no place; Fichte's loyalty is national.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: National independence and strength favour self-reliant defence, but nuclear weapons are anachronistic for the sources, so this is a low-confidence lean.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The leader principle derives authority from charisma and national mission rather than any electoral rule, and the sources are silent on mechanism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking was not discussed in the sources; the Volkisch suspicion of finance gives no clear direction on independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The homeland is sacred soil in Volkisch and Legionary thought, so ceding historic national territory would be abhorrent.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Legion rejected materialist capitalism and Fichte placed the nation above the individual, so property is justified by service to the national whole.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: This is a debate among Marxists; the sources on national mysticism treat the USSR simply as an enemy, so nothing can be stated.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk governance is not in the sources; Volkisch reverence for nature offers only a weak pull.

collective-defense.rationale: An alliance clause is not discussed; the national mystic's emphasis on independence is balanced by the Legion's search for fascist allies.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Consent of annexed peoples is not a theme; national claims to historic land prevail over the principle, but no statement is documented.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Legion wove Orthodoxy into nationalism rather than curbing the church, so subordination of clergy to civil power is not its program, though it is not defended either.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Legion's Captain was a partisan leader, but a symbol standing above party also fits romantic nationalism; the sources do not decide.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Because the nation is an indivisible eternal whole, force to keep a region would be justified in defence of it.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A unitary national community under one law does not make room for regions with their own systems, so this is opposed, though the sources do not discuss it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Legion surrounded its Captain with devotion and monuments and national mysticism sanctifies the nation, but divine descent of the head of state is not documented as a tenet, so adherents are not clearly for or against.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No tax doctrine appears in the sources on the Iron Guard or the Volkisch movement.

character-from-environment.rationale: Volkisch thought treated the Volk's essence as innate and ancestral, though Fichte's national education aimed to form character, so the lean is moderate.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The leader principle treats the leader as the expression of the national will, so he is not bound by earlier laws; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: A question of modern technocratic futurism; the movements rejected scientistic modernity and offer no view on space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Volkisch thinkers imagined a harmonious hierarchy ruled by natural elites, with some primitive democracy, but did not endorse a classical mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Codreanu's commemoration through monuments and gatherings and his charismatic leadership are documented in the Iron Guard article.

equal-parenting.rationale: Courts and custody are not discussed; traditional family ideas would favour mothers as carers, but this is inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This concerns Marxist-Leninist theory, to which national mysticism offers no stance beyond hostility to Marxism.

land-redistribution.rationale: The peasantry is glorified in Volkisch and Legionary writings, so giving land to its tillers fits, but the movements had no worked-out agrarian reform.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not address refugee return; Legionary and Volkisch attachment to homeland might sympathise with return of the nation's own, while others were treated as aliens.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Germanic and Greater Romania strands of Volkisch and Legionary nationalism claimed lands wherever members of the people lived.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Legion was Orthodox and nationalist but did not call for legal punishment of apostasy, and the Volkisch movement included people leaving Christianity.

women-must-cover.rationale: A Muslim-world demand outside the documented concerns of these movements, so no lean exists beyond general traditionalism.

common-currency.rationale: A shared currency across states pools sovereignty, which a sacred nation's adherents oppose; the sources do not say more.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Germanic strands of the Volkisch movement wanted union of kin peoples, but the Legion's focus was on Romania alone, so the lean is slight.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Self-governing institutions for minorities cut against the cultural unity of the Volk, so they are not welcomed; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: A Jewish-history debate not covered by the sources on national mysticism; the Legion and Volkisch antisemites wanted Jews out and so offer no stance on how they should respond.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fichte and the Legion read history as the unfolding of a people's spirit under a divine law, not as a product of economic conditions.

ban-cartels.rationale: The Iron Guard had no consistent economic program, and nothing in the sources addresses competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: No documented position; a national-economy outlook could favour rescuing national firms but the sources never say so.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Volk's will is held to be sovereign over formal institutions, yet 'majority' in liberal terms is not their concept; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Legionary rhetoric centred on masculinity and virility, and women made up only a small share of members, so parity quotas would be rejected.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A communal national economy opposed to international capitalism points toward autarky, but no bloc plan is documented.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding international rules would limit national self-direction, which Fichte's nation-centred outlook resists.

moral-incentives.rationale: The Legion's New Man seeks nothing for himself and its movement is a spiritual school, so duty and sacrifice are the proper motives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Legion's Death Squad and assassinations show a belief that a small devoted band can shape events by sacrificial action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Völkisch nostalgia for the Holy Roman Empire's hierarchical order and belief in natural elites resist abolition; the Legion was anti-aristocratic in part.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Fichte demanded a national education built around the nation's own character, language and destiny.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Racial hierarchy would justify rule over others, but the mystical focus is the nation's own rebirth rather than tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Fichte's Addresses name a thorough national education as the sole means of preserving the German nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposition to measures aiding other groups follows from racial hierarchy, though the issue is anachronistic.

public-money-creation.rationale: Antisemitic suspicion of finance existed in these movements, but money creation is not documented.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Legion rejected capitalism as materialistic but sources give no theory of its crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pan-national ambitions are possible but not documented for mystical nationalism generally.

delink-world-market.rationale: Anti-capitalist national economy might favour withdrawal, but there is no documented program.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist thesis; the Legion opposed Marxism and stressed national unity of classes.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Exclusion of aliens is an aim, but private-property libertarian reasoning is foreign to the movement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal individual-rights constitutionalism was rejected, with universal democratic values called Jewish inventions.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not discussed in the sources on national mysticism; sympathy for national independence gives a faint lean but no documented position.

elective-rulers.rationale: Leadership derived from charisma and heroism rather than election.

minority-veto.rationale: The nation is one whole under a single law of development, leaving no room for dissenting vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Legion fought rulers it deemed illegitimate but its own leader principle is absolute; split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Legion and the DVFP rejected parliamentary politics for a leader-led order.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Völkisch nature reverence may favour it, but there is no documented stance.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Volkisch reverence for nature might favour humane treatment but nothing in the sources states it.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty to the community by the strong fits an organic Volk, but is not specifically documented.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Fichte called the pious recommendation to withdraw from national affairs a gross misuse of religion.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural pessimism about modernity is Völkisch, but this critical theory claim is not.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian cultural hegemony theory was foreign to these movements, which saw politics as a spiritual and racial struggle.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed, though the Legion resented foreign and minority economic dominance.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Iron Guard blamed Jews for blocking Christian Romanians and the Völkisch movement treated outsiders as corrupting, so offices would go to the native nation.

party-own-road.rationale: A question about communist parties' relations; national mystics have no role in it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Fichte told Germans that no outside power would save them and they must help themselves.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Greater national territory was a nationalist aim of the Iron Guard milieu; Romania's inter-war borders were a constant theme.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources do not discuss settler societies; a blood-and-soil Volk might sympathise with rootedness, but the question concerns colonial settler states.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Adherents were themselves radical right nationalists and would reject it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Legion opposed communism fiercely but would not accept being condemned equally.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside the sources for national mysticism and no consistent stance is documented.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Reverence for national ancestors and heritage, as in Fichte and the Volkisch romantics, favours keeping monuments to the nation's past.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed, though the rhetoric of emasculated men touches it.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Legionary rhetoric of virility suggests a particular view of men and women but not this issue.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Fichte held that each nation develops by its own law, so foreign institutions do not suit it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Legion saw itself as guardian of the nation but conflicted with the army and king; split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Volkisch and Legionary rhetoric put women in family roles within the organic community, so paying for domestic work as labour is not a theme.

filial-duty.rationale: Generational continuity of the people and Orthodox family values.

office-by-exam.rationale: Selection by loyalty, character and heroism over formal learning suits movements that distrusted rationalism and intellectuals.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The Legion resented foreign and minority control of the national economy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Orthodox and traditionalist ideals of the family as the cell of the nation lead to opposing easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Authority runs from the leader downward in the Legion, so delegates bound to and removable by those below is contrary to its structure.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Völkisch and Legionary soil mysticism, but land tenure systems not documented.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Both the Legion and the Volkisch right rejected parliament's authority in favour of leadership, so parliament's budget veto is not valued.

single-official-language.rationale: Fichte treated the national language as the heart of the people.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The soil is sacred and tied to the people in Volkisch and Legionary thought, so foreigners owning it would be resisted.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Volkisch racial hierarchy treats group differences as natural, so unequal outcomes would not be considered discriminatory.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Legion rejected capitalism as overly materialistic and pursued spiritual self-purification, which implies a critique of consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The sources do not address covert foreign policy; ultra-nationalist assertiveness gives no clear lean.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Imperial control over allies is not discussed; national mystics emphasise nations' own independence.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-capitalist and anti-plutocratic suspicion runs through the Legion, so corporate sway over government is likely seen as a problem.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Defence of the nation against alien influence leads to restricting foreign money in media and universities; inferred from antisemitic and nativist outlook.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fichte's hope for eternity lies in the continuance of the people.

residents-only-property.rationale: Soil rooted in the local community and the people suggests restrictions on outsiders, but housing policy is not documented.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment policy is not documented in the sources on the Iron Guard or Volkisch movement.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democracy was rejected as a Jewish invention by Codreanu, so spreading it is not seen as a route to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Fichte's nation rests on duty and sacrifice to the whole and the leader principle demands obedience, so there is a general duty.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources on national mysticism do not discuss rules of intervention; national self-assertion may allow intervention when convenient.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed; the Legion was concerned with the nation, not labour organisation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The Iron Guard blamed Jews for Freemasonry, Marxism and rabbinical aggression.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The family is the nation's cell for Volkisch and Orthodox traditionalists, so removing marriage's legal status is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Transparency rights are a liberal concern; a leader-centred movement is unlikely to favour them, but the sources do not say.

local-production.rationale: Glorification of peasants and rural life favours local food and goods, though it is not a stated policy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Fichte's nation as a self-contained order under its own law means its constitution outranks external law.

religious-nation.rationale: The Legion tied the nation to Orthodoxy, but the Völkisch movement was split (Germanised Christianity or paganism).

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A nation of divine origin owes no tribute to another, and Fichte called the Germans an original people.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: National unity of one people implies pooling resources across regions, but the sources do not document fiscal policy.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Personal belongings in a communist economy is a Marxist idea; the sources do not engage it, so no stance is documented.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Legion opposed communism fiercely and blamed Jews for Marxism, so coexistence is not accepted.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Health and service delivery models are not in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Legion inserted strong elements of Orthodox Christianity.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Legion rejected capitalism as overly materialistic and the Volkisch movement opposed industrial evils, so it is not seen as progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist thesis; Volkisch and Legionary traditionalists do not hold that women's equality is a goal.

socialized-care.rationale: The family is the cell of the Volk, so shifting housework and childcare to public services is contrary to the traditional order.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Fichte praised the living German language over languages built on borrowed foundations, which supports linguistic purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Indigenous treaty rights are not discussed in the sources; nationalists' sense of homeland gives no clear lean.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small cooperative communities with common property are an anarchist or utopian ideal, while the Volkisch settlement colonies were racial and agrarian, so the sources give a mild lean against.

majority-settlement.rationale: A programme of settling the majority in minority regions is nationalist in spirit, but the sources do not document it for national mysticism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Legion rejected both capitalism's materialism and communism, seeking a communal national economy as a third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: National mystics hold the soil sacred and tied to ancestors and so give historic tie priority over later residents' claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Iron Guard preceded the war's end and the sources do not record denial positions, so none is documented for the ideology as such.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditionalist and Orthodox morality in these movements suggests moral condemnation, but criminal law is not discussed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Legion used violence against opponents and the DVFP called for a Volkisch dictatorship, so suppressing independent opposition is consistent with its aims.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Legion fused Orthodoxy with nationalism, but legal punishment of blasphemy is not documented, and Volkisch pagans would not support it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial administration is not discussed; national self-interest and racial hierarchy lean toward serving the ruling nation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A concept of Islamic law which these movements do not address, so no stance applies.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious legitimacy to remove rulers is not the Legion's doctrine; it fought regimes as enemies of the nation, not by a jurist's rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Leader-centred movements reject broad participation in favour of leadership by heroes and natural elites.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Racism, sexism and class oppression as linked systems is a progressive theory that Volkisch and Legionary ideology treats as foreign and rejects.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Volkisch and Legionary traditionalism treat sex roles as natural, so legal recognition by gender identity would be rejected.

assisted-dying.rationale: The Orthodox religiosity of the Legion implies opposition, although the sources do not discuss it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Vasile Marin argued the movement was revolutionary left, not right; adherents rejected labels.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's concept is not engaged; the Legion's critique of capitalism was moral and nationalist.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The sources on national mysticism do not discuss Islam; their hostility is aimed at Jews and liberals, so no stance is documented.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Fichte describes a people as arising out of the divine under a special law of development, and national mysticism raises the nation to numen, so authority has a divine root.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious symbols in state institutions are not discussed; the Legion's Orthodox nationalism would tolerate them for the national church.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A contemporary workplace regulation not addressed by the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Legion rejected capitalism but also had no developed economic programme, so this is left open.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Fichte demanded readiness to fight for the nation and the Legion cultivated martial sacrifice, so abolishing forces is rejected.

rich-first.rationale: Economic development sequencing is not in the sources; the Legion's economic views were unsystematic.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Legion's foreign alignment sought to join the fascist powers, but the sources do not describe a general doctrine on blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Leadership by charisma and heroism is favoured over inheritance in the Legion, though Volkisch writers admired the Holy Roman Empire's order, so no clear position.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Credit institutions are not discussed in the sources, though antisemitic resentment of finance existed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Resistance to foreign economic control matches nationalist independence, but the sources do not document the issue.

property-franchise.rationale: Voting rights in these movements follow nation or race rather than property, and the sources do not discuss the franchise by wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist thesis alien to Volkisch and Legionary traditionalism, which treated gender roles as natural.

reification.rationale: A Marxist theory of commodity relations that the sources on national mysticism do not engage.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A socialist critique of press freedom; the Legion did blame minorities for media influence, but the sources do not record this stance.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Government by the leader's decisions rather than fixed laws is the leader principle in action, so rule through general standing law is not a priority.

racial-franchise.rationale: Volkisch thought made the Volk a racial essence and the DVFP wanted dictatorship, so political rights would be tied to membership in the Volk.

online-participation.rationale: A modern participatory-democracy idea that these movements, which rejected broad popular decision, would not support.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency of decision records is a liberal democratic ideal and does not fit leader-centred movements; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Concern for the nation's religious and racial purity, as in the Legion's antisemitism, supports restricting mixed marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The Iron Guard blamed Jews for blocking Christian Romanians' economic advancement, so avoiding Jewish-owned businesses fits.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random citizen deliberation conflicts with rule by heroes and natural elites, but is not discussed directly.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Orthodox traditionalism holds to inherited doctrine rather than modernising it, so reinterpretation is not their approach.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Individual liberty is not the Legion's central concern, though it resented plutocrats; no direct statement is documented.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The Legion's rhetoric centred on virile masculinity as the new man, so open gay service would be rejected.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Legion tied nation and Orthodox faith and national mysticism treats the nation as sacred, so state atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A movement that prized order, discipline and enforcement against enemies would reject abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The nation is one body with one will, so formal power sharing between communities contradicts it.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Organic community care may fit, but the sources do not compare charity with state programs.

term-limits.rationale: Charismatic leadership without fixed limits is the model of the Legion's Captain, so term limits are not favoured.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: A modern effective-altruist concern not in the sources, though the nation's continuity is of supreme importance, which gives no clear mapping.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a modern participatory idea that leader-centred movements would not adopt; this is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Orthodox tradition keeps clergy male and the Legion adopted its religiosity, so women could not hold every office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Traditional family ideals of Volkisch and Orthodox movements assume the husband's headship.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Political membership belongs to the national community defined by ancestry and spirit, so resident aliens would not vote.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not documented in the sources, so nothing can be said.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property law is not addressed by the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Legion was a spiritual school that organised students and youth in uniformed disciplined groups under a Captain, and Fichte wanted the whole nation reshaped by education.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: A modern defence question absent from these movements' sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: National independence and Fichte's insistence on self-reliance suggest resistance to foreign troops, but the sources do not discuss bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Formal recognition of past mass killings runs against a sacred-national outlook that lauded martial sacrifice, though the sources do not discuss recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Legion denounced capitalist materialism and honoured labour, so rewards should follow useful work; stated only loosely in the sources.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism contradicts the Legion's martial sacrifice and Fichte's readiness to fight for the nation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: National mysticism is defined by pseudohistorical claims about a nation's antiquity and origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Volkisch thought sees the Volk and sex as natural essences rooted in nature, so constructivism about sex is rejected.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A post-structural feminist claim at odds with traditionalist views of fixed sex roles in the organic nation.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Legion cultivated a cult of martyrdom and self-sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Codreanu described the Legion as a spiritual school for national rebirth through self-purification toward God.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The sources do not discuss diaspora relations; both a gathering of the nation and a spiritual centre are consistent with national mysticism.

culture-before-state.rationale: Fichte sought national education before political restoration.

god-not-male.rationale: Orthodox Christianity of the Legion uses male terms for God, and a Volkisch pagan strand worshipped gods of both sexes, so the lean is slightly against.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist theological test that Orthodox and Volkisch traditionalists do not accept.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Iron Guard blamed Jews for blocking Christian Romanians' economic advancement.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Greater Romania and pan-German strands wanted all people of one nation in one territorial unit, which matches this.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence is not discussed; the organic national unity ideal would subordinate unions to the nation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist test of socialism that national mystics, who oppose Marxism, do not take part in.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public ownership of local services is not documented in the Legion's unsystematic economic ideas.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not discussed, and rule by natural elites might favour an upper house but the sources do not say.

municipal-property.rationale: Local-community ownership of production is a left-libertarian or municipalist idea; the sources show the Legion favouring nation and peasantry instead.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The nation is a single indivisible whole in Fichte's account, so confederations with no governing power contradict it.

family-wage.rationale: Traditional family ideals with a male breadwinner support a wage for the worker's family, but the sources do not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: A modern regulatory question outside the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: A transhumanist concern not addressed by national mystics.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A modern libertarian technology question outside the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: A modern digital question not addressed by the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Fichte still ranks the nation over the individual, though he denies the nation's glory heals individual injury.

spiritual-nature.rationale: National mysticism elevates the nation to the status of numen, so politics serves a spiritual order.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A unitary national community leaves regional powers as grants from the national government, which can be withdrawn.

gm-crops.rationale: Biotech agriculture is not discussed; Volkisch reverence for nature and peasant life suggests scepticism but nothing documented.

dense-cities.rationale: The Volkisch movement idealised rural regions and opposed industrialisation, so dense cities would be seen as worse.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race is central to Volkisch thought, with the Volk as a racial essence and Aryans at the top, so racial groups are seen as having distinct interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Volkisch writers celebrated the Aryan or German race, so pride in ancestry is legitimate.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Fichte and the Legion celebrated struggle and sacrifice, and pan-nationalist aims included expansion, so limiting force to defence is not accepted.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Fichte treated shared language as the basis of the German nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates are an issue in other settings that the sources do not discuss.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The Iron Guard's conspiratorial worldview saw foreign powers and Jews as plotting against the nation, so such a plot is credible to adherents.

free-public-college.rationale: Fichte wanted national education for all, but tuition policy is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental tax design is not discussed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Fichte's immortality through the nation's continuance makes duty to coming generations central.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources record views on distinct roles for the sexes, not on women's distinct political values, so no clear position follows.

arms-reduction.rationale: Fichte's readiness to fight and the Legion's martial cult make reduction of armaments unattractive, though no policy is stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomacy is not discussed in the sources; secrecy and leader discretion suit leader-centred movements, but nothing documented.

capital-controls.rationale: A national economy shielded from international capitalism suggests control over capital flows, but this is inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Legion kept its own armed squads and street violence, so a ban on non-state armed groups would not suit it.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Fichte demands readiness to die for the nation, so refusing orders to fight in its wars is a betrayal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour relations are not documented for the Legion; organic national harmony over class bargaining is the general ideal.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credit policy is not in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal limits on borrowing are not discussed in the sources.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic reform is not discussed; nation-first outlook gives no stance on developing-country rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Legion wanted to capture and remake the state for the nation rather than abolish its machinery, and Fichte called the state a necessary framework.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: A free choice of economic systems would not fit a single national economy under the nation's guidance, but this is not documented.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Legion was a disciplined hierarchy led by a Captain, and national mysticism seeks a unified national order, so loose informal groups without permanent organisation are not its model.

sacred-nation.rationale: Fichte's Eighth Address bases a person's hope of eternity on the eternal continuance of the people, and national mysticism is defined by raising the nation to the status of numen.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reverence for soil and the spiritual bond of people and land, which resists pricing nature like an asset; the sources do not discuss it.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The movements had no program on education finance and were not centred on economics; no position can be inferred with confidence.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the idea of the nation as one organic, unified body, which treats regional exploitation within it as a betrayal of unity rather than colonialism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from distrust of universalism: the movements located identity in the particular people, not a common humanity, though the question of redesigning nature went unaddressed.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from distrust of liberal pluralism and a preference for national-spiritual direction of culture; independent public media was not a topic for these movements.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from its sanctification of the nation and often a particular national faith, such as Orthodoxy in the Iron Guard, over universalism.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from its glorification of peasant soil and people; the Legion drew heavily on the peasantry.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its stress on national strength and distrust of universalism.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from its placing of the nation above class, which rejects class-based parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred weakly and not discussed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' organic, traditional views point both ways.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from Fichte's view of a shared language as the living bond of the nation.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from its distrust of liberal individualism and preference for state and national duty over private suits.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from its organic, traditional hierarchy and hostility to liberal democracy.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from its sanctification of soil and its priority of duty and sacrifice over individual interest.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its authoritarian, anti-liberal stance favouring firm national discipline.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its view of language as the core of the nation, so settlers must adopt it.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Mystical nationalists wrote little on labour policy; the Legion had no economic program, so no position is documented.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by Fichte, the Volkisch writers or the Legion; no position can be documented.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Legion fused nation and Orthodox faith and the Volkisch movement favoured a national religiosity, so the nation's own tradition would hold precedence; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Volkisch movement called for a dictatorship and the Legion rejected liberal democracy and party politics, so free competitive elections are not what makes a state legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: The Legion's spiritual rebirth and New Man ideal stressed purity and duty, and the Volkisch movement prized traditional rural family life; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The movements put the national community and order above individual liberty and would accept state control of communications; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The Iron Guard had no economic program and prized a peasant ideal and spiritual over material aims, so a bureaucratic cash-transfer scheme is not their position; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Volkisch and Legionary movements were anti-liberal and patriarchal in their ideal of the national family; inferred, not stated.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: These movements held religion or sacred tradition to be the nation's foundation, not a source of oppression; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The Volkisch movement was built on a mystical Volk and a racial hierarchy, treating races as real natural groupings.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the movements' patriarchal ideal of the national family and distrust of liberal universalism.

missingStatements.text: The nation is a sacred community that outlasts its individual members and gives their lives lasting meaning.
missingStatements.rationale: Fichte's Eighth Address bases a person's hope of eternity on the eternal continuance of the people, and national mysticism is defined by raising the nation to the status of numen.

missingStatements.text: Citizens' highest duty is to be ready to die for their nation.
missingStatements.rationale: Fichte says a man must be ready even to die that the nation may live, and the Legion cultivated a cult of martyrdom and self-sacrifice through its Death Squad.

notes: The Volkisch strand split between Germanising Christianity and reviving Germanic paganism, and the Legion was Orthodox Christian, so religion statements mix. The Legion lacked a consistent economic program, so economic answers are mostly low-confidence.
